# ModDotPlot Browser v0.8.8

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

v0.8.8 makes the first-run path easier to evaluate and adds plot-spanning pointer
guides for comparing distant rows and columns. The landing page now identifies optional
FAI/GZI companion files as the faster loading path and can launch a bundled
*Arabidopsis thaliana* genome plus centromere annotation in one step. Interactive plots
show dotted horizontal and vertical guides at the pointer by default; Advanced options
can hide them, rotate them to diagonals, or change their stroke pattern.

See the [validation record](v0.8.8/VALIDATION.md) for the release checks on this
isolated source copy.

## Bundled Arabidopsis example

Select **Try ModDotPlot on an Arabadopsis genome** below the ordinary landing controls
to load the included `Col-CEN_v1.2.fasta` sequence and `ColCEN_CEN180.gff3` annotation.
The matching `Col-CEN_v1.2.fasta.fai` companion is also bundled so record metadata can
be published through the v0.8.7 indexed-input path. Once the example is viewable, the
application enters the normal workspace automatically; no local file selection is
required.

These files are static release assets. Choosing the example retrieves them from the
same origin that serves the application, so hosts should account for their size when
deploying or caching this release. User-selected sequence and annotation files retain
the existing browser-local processing behavior.

## Cursor guides

Moving the pointer over an interactive Self or Pairwise plot displays two guides that
cross at the pointer. The initial geometry is one horizontal and one vertical line,
and the initial stroke is dotted. The overlay follows display coordinates only: it
does not change genomic coordinates, tile calculation, hover values, exports, or the
underlying scientific data.

Advanced options provide three independent choices:

* disable or enable the guide overlay;
* use horizontal/vertical guides or crossing diagonal guides; and
* render the lines as dotted, dashed, or solid.

The overlay applies to the full interactive plot. Grid overviews retain their existing
cell-selection and axis-reordering interactions.

## Landing-page wording

The optional-index hint now explicitly notes that FAI/GZI companions provide faster
loading. The supported combinations and validation rules are unchanged: plain FASTA
uses FAI, BGZF FASTA uses FAI plus GZI, and ordinary gzip remains on the eager path.

## Compatibility

Scientific estimation, exact rendering, grid semantics, indexed/eager ingestion,
annotation parsing, and export formats are unchanged from v0.8.7. The complete v0.8.7
source remains beside this release for direct comparison and rollback.
